title.narrative: Mine Action support to humanitarian activities for the most vulnerable populations in Syria

description.narrative: ltpgtExplosive ordnance contamination remains a major protection concern, dangerously affecting the lives and livelihoods of the Syrian population. The widespread explosive contamination continues to threaten lives, hamper access to basic services, impedes returnees and obstructs the delivery of humanitarian assistance and the efforts of the international community towards building resilience and early recovery. According to the Humanitarian Situation Report No.6 (as at 27 May 2025), the key highlight was that explosive hazards continue to threaten civilians, with more than 1,000 casualties reported due to explosive ordnance since 8 December 2024. The same report also states that a key barrier to returns of IDPs is the threat of unexploded ordnance. According to the 2024 Humanitarian Needs Overview (HNO), no comprehensive and nationwide survey has been conducted to determine the extent of the explosive ordnance contamination, and such a survey has not yet taken place in 2025.ltbrgtMine action response activities are key enablers to the delivery of humanitarian aid, services, and early recovery to assist people inltbrgtneed, as well as a prerequisite to safe, dignified and voluntary return. Mine action is a comprehensive approach which requires sustained and flexible funding and mine action mainstreaming supports planning of all sectors through provision of contamination data andltbrgtenables safe activities by promoting life-saving behaviors through risk education, mitigating and removing threats by survey and clearance. Yet, while delivery of explosive ordnance risk education and awareness messages is widespread, survey and clearance remain geographically limited and underfunded.ltbrgtThrough this project, NPA will deploy local non-technical survey (NTS), explosive ordnance risk education (EORE) and clearance teams in Rural Damascus and Homs Governorates, within all of the nine SHF prioritised locations. They will conduct contamination survey, spot clearance, and provide a rapid response to explosive ordnance call-out capability. This project not only aims to support those most at threat within the targeted areas, but also to provide technical mine action services to other humanitarian organisations to support the performance of their projects. This will complement the service UNMAS provides to UN entities, to which non-UN actors have limited or no access. Since March 2025, NPA has conducted mine action services to support INGOs in the WASH and Health sectors for the clearance of irrigation canals and areas surrounding medical clinics. Both projects had faced delays in implementation due to the lack of mine action technical support. NPA’s experience collaborating with INGOs in other sectors and the need for mine action to enable effective humanitarian support has driven the design of this project. ltbrgtThe project activities will directly support the Syrian Humanitarian Fund First Standard Allocation 2025 – Envelope 2 – Supporting Safe and Dignified Return from Areas of Displacement to Areas of Origin: Returnees and communities in areas of origin have equitable access to protection, essential services, and livelihoods, enabling safe, voluntary, and dignified return”. In addition, the project will integrate a referral protocol for services beyond the scope of this project, via the deployment of an NTS team and a dedicated community liaison capacity, to other humanitarian actors in areas of Gender Based Violence, education, Housing Land and Property (HLP) and WASH. The referral process will be via email and phone communications between NPA and the relevant humanitarian actors.ltbrgtNPA adheres to the humanitarian principles of humanity, neutrality, impartiality, and independence in its mine action programming and firmly believes in the need to assess and monitor activities to ensure that they contribute positively to social unity and cohesion and do not contribute to further conflict – the ‘Do No Harm’ principle.ltbrgtlt/pgt
